edges.target: Bootstrap significance test (Efron & Tibshirani)
edges.ref: [113] B. Efron and R. J. Tibshirani, An Introduction to the Bootstrap, Chapman & Hall/CRC, 1993
edges.evidence: For this, we use bootstrapping [113] to resample to estimate the distributions, estimate confidence intervals, and check that if their differences are just chance.

edges.target: K-Means++ seeding (Arthur & Vassilvitskii)
edges.ref: [109] D. Arthur and S. Vassilvitskii, k-means++: The advantages of careful seeding, SODA 2007
edges.evidence: LINE uses the K-Means++ centroid finder [109]: Given already selected rows S, a new row x is chosen with probability proportional to D(x,S)^2

edges.target: Tree of Parzen Estimators as design template for LITE (Bergstra)
edges.ref: [110] J. Bergstra and Y. Bengio, Random search for hyper-parameter optimization, JMLR 13(2), 2012
edges.evidence: LITE was inspired by Bergstra's Tree of Parzen Estimators [110]. It was an experiment in simplifying TPE and adapting it to fixed pools.

edges.target: Fastmap (Faloutsos & Lin)
edges.ref: [118] C. Faloutsos and K.-I. Lin, FastMap: A fast algorithm for indexing, data-mining and visualization, ACM 1995
edges.evidence: Fastmap [118], a Nystrom-like method that derives components from distant "corners" (k). In operation, it picks a random row r; then selects row k1 far from r.

edges.target: Aha's distance for mixed data
edges.ref: [119] D. W. Aha, D. Kibler, M. K. Albert, Instance-based learning algorithms, Mach. Learn. 6, 1991
edges.evidence: For mixed data (numbers/symbols), Fastmap uses Aha's distance [119]: Numbers: dist(x,y)=|x-y| (normalized 0..1). Symbols: dist(x,y)=0 if x=y, else 1.

edges.target: DBSCAN minPts guideline (Schubert et al.)
edges.ref: [115] E. Schubert, J. Sander, M. Ester, H.-P. Kriegel, X. Xu, DBSCAN revisited, revisited, ACM TODS 42(3), 2017
edges.evidence: Following DBSCAN guidelines [115], line 10 of Algorithm 1 requires filled buckets to contain at least 2d minPts rows.

edges.target: Epsilon-domination (Deb et al.)
edges.ref: [88] K. Deb, M. Mohan, S. Mishra, Evaluating the epsilon-domination based multi-objective evolutionary algorithm, Evolutionary Computation 13(4), 2005
edges.evidence: The second assumption follows Deb et al.'s epsilon domination criteria [88], where epsilon divides the problem space into hypercubes requiring only one sample per cube.

edges.target: Hoeffding's inequality sample bound
edges.ref: [91] W. Hoeffding, Probability inequalities for sums of bounded random variables, JASA 58(301), 1963

edges.target: Reference-optimal terminology (McGeoch; Cohen)
edges.ref: [40] C. C. McGeoch, A Guide to Experimental Algorithmics, CUP 2012; [41] P. R. Cohen, Empirical methods for AI, MIT Press 1995
edges.evidence: Here, "optimal" means "reference optimal," (which is a term from empirical algorithms literature [40, 41]). The reference optimal refers to the best solution observed so far.

edges.target: Pool-based vs membership-query taxonomy (Settles)
edges.ref: [99] B. Settles, Active learning, Synthesis Lectures on AI and ML, 2012
edges.evidence: Optimization strategies can differ between pool-based and membership query inference [99]. Pool-based methods search existing datasets, while membership query methods interpolate

edges.target: PriorBand (Mallik et al.) considered and rejected
edges.ref: [121] N. Mallik et al., PriorBand: practical hyperparameter optimization in the age of deep learning, NeurIPS 2023
edges.evidence: PriorBand is specifically tailored for deep learning applications (which are not studied here). Hence, for this study, we chose to remain with DEHB.

edges.target: Traditional text mining beats deep learners and runs 100x faster for agile effort (Tawosi et al.)

edges.target: K-Means pre-clustering 500+ times faster than deep learning for defect prediction (Majumder et al.)

edges.target: Tree-based models beat DNNs on tabular data, especially >10,000 samples (Grinsztajn et al.)

not_reuse_examples: [114] Nemenyi: named only as the test Scott-Knott is preferred over; not applied.
[101][104][105][106] Hyperband / successive halving / differential evolution / Hyperopt: described as components or comparators inside DEHB, not run separately as baselines.
[116][117] Zhu manifold survey / Pearson PCA: background in Table 4; PCA not run (Fastmap used instead).
[50]-[67] history-of-simplicity list (PCA, JL lemma, backdoors, distillation ...): background timeline only.
[72][73] Ling et al. data synthesis / Fu & Menzies easy-over-hard: qualitative motivation, no number or method adopted.
[81]-[87] label-quality and SZZ literature: background on labeling problems, nothing adopted.
[95][96][97] Apel / Zhou / Zapotecas-Martinez: background quotes on configurability and multi-objective definition.
[131] Zhou et al. prompt search: future work only.
https://github.com/KKGanguly/NEO: the paper's own replication package, not reuse.
notes: Retyped Hoeffding [91] and Jin [92] to theory and Hou [42] to numericfact; added 10 numericfact premises (22.5 CPU years, 5%, 500x, 100x, 4:1, 90%, 10-30%, >10K rows, labeling hours, knobs figure), geometric-waiting-time theory [89], and the [122] 'trivially small' critique the paper rebuts (refutes); no replication edges exist; [94] personal communication is also mis-cited for the stars-in-universe claim; threats section says N=39 while Table 1 says 127; LITE's TPE inspiration cites Bergstra's random-search paper [110] not the TPE paper.
